problem: Multi-hop KBQA lacks supervision signals at intermediate steps; algorithms get feedback only from the final answer, which "makes the learning unstable or ineffective" (abstract).
method: A teacher-student approach. The student (Neural State Machine) finds the answer; the teacher learns intermediate entity distributions using both forward and backward reasoning, producing intermediate supervision signals that are used to improve the student. Teacher architectures include parallel and hybrid 3-hop reasoning variants.
key_assumptions: Training data is only <question, answer> pairs, so intermediate path supervision must be inferred rather than read off
The intermediate entity distributions produced by the bidirectional teacher are reliable enough to supervise the student
Correcting spurious intermediate reasoning is the main lever for improving multi-hop accuracy
main_contribution: First explicit learning of intermediate supervision signals with a teacher-student framework via bidirectional reasoning, alleviating spurious reasoning and improving KBQA especially where training data is lacking.
results: Evaluation casts multi-hop KBQA as ranking, using Hits@1 and F1. Per the authors' repo table, NSM reaches WebQSP 68.7, MetaQA-1hop 97.1, MetaQA-2hop 99.9, MetaQA-3hop 98.9, CWQ 47.6, with the teacher-student variant reported as NSM+p (73.9 on WebQSP) in the README excerpt. The authors note most methods do very well on MetaQA-1hop and MetaQA-2hop and that the challenge is at greater depth.
limitations: Supervision is an intermediate ENTITY DISTRIBUTION over the question-specific graph, not natural-language or passage context around a fact.
Requires a bounded question-specific subgraph (2-hop for WebQSP, 4-hop for CWQ) and reasoning steps set per dataset (4 for CWQ, 3 otherwise), so depth is a hyperparameter.
MetaQA 1/2-hop are nearly saturated (99.9), so headroom for the idea's context-enrichment claim on those splits is minimal.
future_work: not stated in the passages read
code_availability: Available and verified: https://github.com/RichardHGL/WSDM2021_NSM (Python/PyTorch, 149 stars, includes main_nsm.py / main_teacher.py / main_student.py, run_metaqa.sh / run_webqsp.sh / run_CWQ.sh, paper DOI 10.1145/3437963.3441753, arXiv id 2101.03737 in README).

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: The idea's 'adaptive repair loop that detects one-hop failures and generates corrective examples' is conceptually adjacent to this paper's intermediate-supervision learning, but the paper derives intermediate supervision from a differentiable teacher over entity distributions, whereas the idea proposes detecting concrete one-hop failures and regenerating training examples. The paper also provides the hop-stratified MetaQA evaluation (1/2/3-hop) that the idea needs for its 'transfer to deeper queries' claim.
relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.65: both target multi-hop KBQA with poor intermediate supervision, a core motivation of the idea's repair loop. Method overlap 0.35: teacher-student intermediate supervision is a different mechanism from passage-context data enrichment plus example regeneration; it corrects reasoning signals rather than enriching the supervision text. Evaluation overlap 0.6: MetaQA-1/2/3-hop and WebQSP/CWQ with Hits@1/F1 are exactly the benchmark family the idea would use to measure hop-depth transfer.
